final_answer:
MEMORANDUM (privileged; to D. Arroyo; 4/25/2025): Section 1033 impact on Elara, Verdant, Trellispoint agreements

1. BOTTOM LINE
- All three agreements fail Rule requirements on authorization, reauthorization, retention/deletion and downstream/secondary use; Trellispoint is highest risk. FNB is not a Bank Innovation Alliance member; plan to April 1, 2027 (Tier 2), no breathing room.
- Three premises in the assignment materials are wrong and change strategy: (a) Elara non-renewal notice is 90 days (Elara 15.2), not 180 (180 days is the convenience-termination period, 15.3); the deadline is May 16, 2025, not missed; (b) Trellispoint's $1.5M fee attaches only to termination "prior to the expiration of the Initial Term" (8.4), so a notice of April 1, 2026 effective April 1, 2027 should not trigger it; (c) Verdant auto-renews for one year unless non-renewal notice is given 90 days before expiry (12.2): December 2, 2026, so it is not "locked in" only to March 2, 2027, but also risks renewal to March 2, 2028.
- Trellispoint hard dates: non-renewal notice by November 19, 2025 (8.2) or the contract renews to November 19, 2027.
Authority note: Rule citations are from memory; eCFR/CFPB sites were blocked, so rule text is unverified; Pennbrook to confirm, and post-April 2025 developments to be rechecked.

2. REGULATORY CONTEXT
- Tier 2 date April 1, 2027 (checklist III.9; 12 CFR 1033.121, unverified). Checklist's four tiers are simplified; confirm Fidelis National Bank's own assets.
- Injunction: Bank Innovation Alliance v. CFPB, No. 24-cv-01843 (E.D. Ky. Mar. 28, 2025) protects only members; FNB is not covered. Sources conflict on scope (minutes: developer-interface and authorization-disclosure provisions, statutory authority; checklist: procedural challenges); obtain the order. The checklist's "Director Rohit Chandra" and "Spring 2025 Supervisory Highlights" are unverified. Rule may change: draft amendments to be rule-agnostic ("Applicable Data-Access Law" plus stated minimum standards) so they survive vacatur.
- NC Bulletin 2025-03 (Feb. 20, 2025) is non-binding for a national bank (OCC primary). Tier 1 exams start Q2 2026; OCC Bulletin 2023-17 (third-party risk) independently requires oversight of Trellispoint-type relationships.

3. CROSS-CUTTING GAPS (all three)
- Authorization: none requires a standalone, itemized disclosure naming recipients, revocation and one-year expiry (Elara 4.1/Ex. B 14-page ToS clickwrap; Verdant 5.1 one sentence; Trellispoint 4.1/4.4 credential entry via 340 clients). HIGH.
- Duration: perpetual authorization (Elara 4.3; Verdant 5.3; Trellispoint 4.3). Rule: one-year maximum with affirmative reauthorization. HIGH; FNB also needs tracking infrastructure.
- Revocation/deletion/retention: see per-agreement. HIGH/MEDIUM.
- No contractual change-in-law amendment right except Verdant 15.3; all amendments need counterparty signature (Elara 18.4; Verdant 17.2; Trellispoint 15.2).
- Rule covers Regulation E and Z accounts; no agreement addresses credit cards; confirm FNB's covered-account inventory (unverified).

4. SCREEN-SCRAPING TRANSITION AND CONTRACTUAL OBSTACLES
- Rule position (checklist III.1; Whitfield, minutes): once a compliant interface exists FNB may deny credential-based access. Obstacles exist only by contract:
 - Trellispoint: FNB may not deploy CAPTCHA, bot detection, IP blocking or rate limiting (2.1); scraping is exclusive (2.2); FNB has no API duty (2.5); scope auto-expands (3.2); credentials storage consented (2.3). Real contractual right to continue until termination/expiry.
 - Elara: FNB "shall not intentionally block, throttle or interfere" with scraping unless degradation, written rate limits or out-of-scope data (3.2); migration is non-binding (3.3). Partial right; FNB can use 3.2(i)-(iii) and rate limits now.
 - Verdant: no non-interference covenant; credentialed access is the "sole method" (2.4), FNB must use commercially reasonable efforts to keep the portal available (2.5), and it may issue technical guidelines (2.2). No API right exists, so amendment is needed to onboard Verdant to the interface; a unilateral cutoff invites a 2.5/9.2 dispute (low-medium).
- Path: (1) sandbox and documentation by Q4 2026; (2) amendment requiring interface use, 90-day migration, then credential access ends on a stated cutover date (not later than April 1, 2027); (3) written rate limits now (Elara); (4) FNB should evaluate removing SSN-last-4, DOB and wealth links from profile pages (Trellispoint 3.1(d)-(e)), since 2.1 bars only blocking measures; (5) Crestline must build and permit rate-limiting; its agreement expires December 31, 2027, nine months post-deadline, so negotiate Rule support and extension now.

5. ELARA (agreement dated 8/15/2021; term through 8/14/2025)
Renewal: 90-day non-renewal deadline May 16, 2025 (Elara 15.2); next windows May 16, 2026 (for 8/14/2026). Either party may also terminate on 180 days' notice any time (15.3): serving by October 3, 2026 ends the agreement by April 1, 2027. Renewal therefore gives little leverage. Recommendation: no non-renewal (it would end API access and $216K revenue before an interface exists); instead send Elara a written Rule-change notice and amendment term sheet in June 2025, diary May 16, 2026 as the protective non-renewal date, and 15.3 as backstop.
Gaps/fixes:
- 5.1(d) (checklist wrongly cites "4(d)") permits marketing lending/insurance using transaction, balance and FNB Credit Score data; targeted advertising and cross-selling are prohibited (12 CFR 1033.421(a), unverified). HIGH. Delete 5.1(d); revise 5.1(b)-(c) to product-necessary uses; 10.3 derived-data ownership to exclude covered-data-derived products; 8.2 anonymized indefinite retention narrowed.
- 4.1/4.3/Ex. B consent: replace with standalone disclosure per Rule, one-year expiry, reauthorization workflow; strike Elara's unilateral right to change consent text. HIGH.
- 8.1 five-year retention; 9.2 deletion after 90 business days plus 12-month backup retention (about 16 months): amend to delete within 30-45 days of revocation or expiry, backups included, with officer certification on request. HIGH.
- 9.1 revocation by email to Elara only, 5 business days: require in-app revocation plus FNB dashboard revocation, cessation within 1 business day. MEDIUM.
- 6.1-6.3: "commercially reasonable" security; no audit rights; 72-hour incident notice; add SOC 2 Type II/ISO 27001/NIST CSF, annual reports, audit rights, keep 72 hours. MEDIUM.
- 2.2(f) FNB Credit Score: checklist treats as excluded confidential commercial information (12 CFR 1033.221, unverified; rule text may address the algorithm rather than outputs). Remove from default scope; any continued sharing under separate voluntary license with fair-lending review. MEDIUM.
- 14.1 cap equals 12 months' fees (about $216K), except indemnity/confidentiality: raise or carve out data-security and Rule-compliance breaches. MEDIUM.
- 3.1 lets FNB discontinue the non-FDX Connect API on 60 days' notice: use at cutover.
Fees: per-call fee ($0.003 x 72M = $216K) is not permissible for interface access under 12 CFR 1033.301(c) (unverified); relabeling is not allowed (checklist III.7). It may be charged until the compliance date, ceasing April 1, 2027 (FY2027 loss about $162K; run-rate $216K; 100% loss). 7.2 scraping is already free. Only separate bona fide commercial arrangements (Whitfield) survive, structured with outside counsel.

6. VERDANT (3/3/2022; expires 3/2/2027)
Termination: cause only, 60-day cure with extended cure (12.3); no convenience right. Non-renewal notice 90 days before expiry = December 2, 2026 (12.2) or renewal to 3/2/2028. Send by mid-November 2026.
Leverage and fallbacks if Verdant will not negotiate:
- 15.3 change-in-law: send notice now; 90-day good-faith negotiation, but neither side need accept an economic change (amendments here are not economic, so Verdant's refusal is weak); afterwards parties "retain all rights" only.
- Material-breach theory is weak before April 1, 2027: Verdant compliance-with-law covenants (9.1(e), 9.3(b), 15.1) bind to current law, and Rule duties on third parties attach at FNB's interface go-live. Stronger breach hooks: 8.3 sharing with unspecified "business partners" without consumer authorization (if Rule obligations are live), 4.1(c) risk modeling; demand the 8.3 Downstream Recipient list now, 5.1 consent records and 3.3 access logs (audit now).
- Fallback: expiry at 3/2/2027 (30 days pre-deadline) is manageable because the Rule obligation is FNB's duty to offer the interface, not Verdant's contract; Verdant's access ends with the contract or on a cutover date, and Verdant may then onboard as an ordinary authorized third party under interface terms. No cutoff before expiry without legal sign-off (2.5 risk).
Gaps: 5.1 one-line consent; 5.3 perpetual; 7.1 seven-year retention and 12.4(b)/(c) (return/destroy within 90 days, credentials 5 business days) with no consumer-revocation deletion (HIGH); 8.3 Downstream Recipients incl. Business Partners without consumer consent (HIGH); 4.1(c) de-identified modeling (MEDIUM); caps $5M per incident/$2M non-indemnity (10.2, 11.2; LOW). Security is the benchmark (PCI-DSS L1, SOC 2 Type II, 48-hour notice): keep 48 hours rather than adopting the checklist's 72-hour benchmark.

7. TRELLISPOINT (11/20/2019; First Amendment 6/1/2022; term to 11/19/2026) - HIGH
- Gaps: exclusive scraping with no-block covenant (2.1-2.5); credential storage (2.3); SSN-4, DOB, brokerage and "any" displayed data (3.1(d)-(f), 3.2); no authorization duty on Trellispoint (4.2, 4.4), perpetual (4.3); data licensing, market research and unrestricted de-identified sale (5.1(b)-(c), 5.2); downstream sharing to about 340 clients with undisclosed contract terms (5.3); retention by Trellispoint policy (6.1); no consumer revocation (6.3; 60-day "commercially reasonable efforts" deletion carve-outs, 6.2); no audit right (10.4); NY law/AAA New York (13). Every checklist category fails.
- Downstream visibility: FNB cannot verify authorization for any client (1.2, 4.2, 5.3); under the Rule each recipient needs its own disclosure and consent, so continuing past April 1, 2027 is not defensible. Interim: demand client list, consent records and retention policy (10.4 summary right).
- Amendment quirk: First Amendment deleted 10.3 and inserted "Section 12A" (misplaced numbering); indemnity cap rose to $3.5M per incident for Trellispoint (FNB $2M), and indemnity is carved out of the $504K liability cap (11.1, 11.3), partly answering the minutes' concern. Indemnity covers third-party claims only (9.1).
- Termination decision matrix (fees at $42K/mo; escalator up to 5% on anniversaries, 7.2):
 A. Non-renewal notice by November 19, 2025 (send by October 31): expires November 19, 2026; ETF $0 on better reading (expiry is not termination without cause; 8.5 distinguishes them); pays about 18.7 months of fees from April 28, 2025 (about $0.8M); access ceases 30 days later (8.5(a)), before interface go-live: coordinate. RECOMMENDED.
 B. No non-renewal; 12-month termination notice by April 1, 2026 effective April 1, 2027: ETF $0 if "prior to expiration" is read by effective date; Trellispoint may argue notice date, exposure $1.5M; adds about 4.4 months of fees beyond A; if notice missed, contract auto-renews to November 19, 2027.
 C. Terminate effective before November 19, 2026 (e.g., notice June 1, 2025): ETF $1.5M; saves under about 6 months of fees (about $250K): reject.
 D. For cause (8.3, 90-day cure): only with a documented breach; uncertain, litigated in AAA New York.
 E. Negotiated exit: mutual termination aligned to interface go-live, fee step-down, Trellispoint as an ordinary authorized aggregator, waiver of ETF, data deletion certificates. Negotiate in parallel with A.
- Economics: $504K/yr to be scraped is inverted (checklist III.7; payments not expressly prohibited). After A, savings of $504K/yr recur; the $1.5M ETF would take about three years of savings to recover.

8. FINANCIAL IMPACT (FNB; preliminary; budget workbook referenced in the 4/10 email was not in my file set, so figures use the minutes)
- Build $2.8M one-time; maintenance $600K/yr. Elara revenue loss $216K/yr from April 1, 2027. Trellispoint savings $504K/yr after exit. Net recurring cost about $312K/yr; five-year cumulative about $4.36M ($2.8M plus $1.56M), excluding legal fees, Crestline integration fees, consent/reauthorization/deletion operations and any ETF (+$1.5M worst case).

9. TIMELINE (backward from April 1, 2027)
- May 1, 2025 Crestline outreach; May 15 budget and risk assessment; May 16 Elara 15.2 deadline; June 2025 Verdant 15.3 notice and Elara/Trellispoint term sheets; Q3 2025 budget approval; October 31, 2025 Trellispoint non-renewal sent (deadline November 19); Q4 2025 specifications; build start no later than January 2026 (12-14 months means March-June 2027 completion, which leaves zero float; start earlier); April 1, 2026 last Trellispoint termination-notice date if A missed; May 16, 2026 Elara non-renewal window; Q3-Q4 2026 testing, 90-day migration; October 3, 2026 last Elara 15.3 notice; November 19, 2026 Trellispoint expiry; December 2, 2026 Verdant non-renewal deadline; March 2, 2027 Verdant expiry; April 1, 2027 compliance.

10. OTHER RED FLAGS AND NEXT STEPS
- Document discrepancies: minutes misname agreements; notice address 400 South Tryon vs 410 in the 4/10 email; Trellispoint notice email legal@fidelisbank.com differs from fnbcorp.com; signature blocks unsigned; checklist dated April 11 but email of April 10 relies on it and the checklist uses April 14 data. Obtain executed copies; confirm notice addresses (Elara 18.1; Verdant 17.6; Trellispoint 15.4) before serving.
- Actions: Whitfield confirms Rule cites and drafts amendments; Lindahl authorization workflows; Kressel scraping risk quantification; limit circulation (privilege).
